title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
interviewAnswer: MCP standardizes how AI applications discover and invoke external tools/resources through a common protocol, reducing one-off integrations between assistants and services.
why: MCP is increasingly relevant for AI engineering because it standardizes how compatible AI clients discover and interact with external tools/resources.
intuition: Instead of writing a custom integration separately for every AI client, an MCP server exposes capabilities through a common protocol that clients can discover and invoke.
deepDive: MCP separates clients from servers that expose tools/resources/prompts through a standardized interface. It does not replace authorization, business logic or tool safety; those still belong in the server/application. Transport and deployment details can vary. The value is interoperability and a consistent contract, not making LLM outputs inherently more reliable.
workedExample: A forecasting application can expose “get_forecast” and “get_reorder_point” through MCP so multiple compatible assistants can use the same deterministic backend tools.
commonMistakes: Describing MCP as a model or vector database.
Assuming MCP automatically grants safe access to every tool.
Exposing internal tools without authentication/permission checks.
followUps: What does an MCP server expose?
Why use MCP for an internal tool ecosystem?
production: Treat MCP servers as production APIs: authenticate clients, validate arguments, rate-limit, log tool calls and version capability contracts.
